question.:question/problem: Let $u = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ -2\end{bmatrix}$ and $v = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$. Given that $u⊥v$ and $x > 0$, find the value of $x$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $u⊥v$ ($u$ and $v$ are perpendicular) if and only if $u\cdot v=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v &={u}_{x}\cdot {v}_{x}+{u}_{y}\cdot {v}_{y} \\  &=x\cdot x+(-2)\cdot 2 \\  &={x}^{2}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v &=0 \\ {x}^{2}-4 &=0 \\ {x}^{2} &=4 \\ x &=\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the negative solution since we are told that $x>0.$ Therefore, $x=2.$
